guideposts.label: From Monaco to Manosque
guideposts.detail: After yesterday’s ITT in the streets of Monaco, today marks the 12th Grand Tour stage starting from the Principality: 9 in the Tour de France, 2 in La Vuelta, 1 in the Giro. Tadej Pogacar won the last two Grand Tour stages starting from Monaco: stage 21 of the Tour 2024, stage 1 of La Vuelta 26. Both stages were ITTs. Manosque is a stage town for the first time in La Vuelta. It has been on the map

guideposts.label: White jersey
guideposts.detail: For the second year in a row, the first leader of the young riders standings is British, as Josh Tarling follows in the footsteps of Ethan Vernon. It was also the case in 2022, when Ethen Hayter took the first four white jerseys before handing it to Fred Wright for one day. This is Tarling’s first distinctive jersey in a Grand Tour.

guideposts.label: Team standings
guideposts.detail: With Tadej Pogacar (1st), Jay Vine (13th) and Ivo Oliveira (14th) in the first positions, UAE Emirates XRG had the best collective performance yesterday. They lead the team standings ahead of Visma-Lease a Bike (+3’’) and Decathlon CMA CGM (+7’’).

guideposts.label: A special day for Molard: "I have some lovely memories"
guideposts.detail: Rudy Molard (Groupama-FDJ United) lives in Tourette-sur-Loup, close to Nice, studied in Barcelonnette and raced around Manosque in the youth categories: “Today, you could say I’m the local rider for this stage, especially as the start is actually going to be very close to my home. We’ll be on my training routes during the first part of the stage. We’re heading into a department I know well, the 04

guideposts.label: First attacks
guideposts.detail: Three riders rapidly opened a gap but they were immediately caught. Now two attackers are riding 17'' ahead of the bunch.

guideposts.label: 15 kilometres into the stage
guideposts.detail: The battle for the first breakaway of La Vuelta 26 goes on. We are experiencing technical difficulties and are working on resolving them to bring you the most accurate and complete coverage of the race.

guideposts.label: 2 leaders, Hayter and Fernandez in pursuit
guideposts.detail: After 25 kilometres of racing, Koen Bouwman (Jayco AlUla) and Diego Uriarte (Kern Pharma) lead the way. Second in GC, Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) is 15 seconds behing them. Then, Sinhué Fernandez (Burgos-Burpellet-BH) trails by 1'20''. Visma-Lease a Bike drives the bunch with a gap of 3'20''.

guideposts.label: Hayter makes it 3 leaders
guideposts.detail: Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) has now bridged the gap to the lead duo. Sinhué Fernandez (Burgos-Burpellet-BH) moves closer: 55 seconds. The gap to the bunch is down to 2'30''.

guideposts.label: The gaps decrease
guideposts.detail: Sinhué Fernandez (Burgos-Burpellet-BH) is 20 seconds behind the three leaders, while the peloton trail by 2 minutes.

guideposts.label: Results at Alto Châteauneuf-Grasse (km 32.3)
guideposts.detail: 1. Bouwman, 3 pts 2. Uriarte, 2 pts 3. Hayter, 1 pt The winner of the KOM standings at the Giro 2022, Koen Bouwman (Jayco AlUla) is set to chase the polka dots again.

guideposts.label: Fernandez also joins the break
guideposts.detail: Make it 4 leaders as the race visits Grasse, the hometown of Giblert Bellone, winner of stage 8 of La Vuelta in 1967. The peloton trail by 1'40''.

guideposts.label: 43.1 km in the first hour
guideposts.detail: And the battle goes on as Visma-Lease a Bike want to keep a tight leash on the four attackers, especially Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step).

guideposts.label: The situation settles
guideposts.detail: At km 60, the peloton are 1'55'' behind Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step), Koen Bouwman (Jayco AlUla), Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) and Diego Uriarte (Kern Pharma).

guideposts.label: Some stats about Pogacar and his first day with La Roja
guideposts.detail: A winner of the Tour de France and the Giro, Pogacar has now led all three Grand Tours (71 Maillot Jaune, 20 Maglia Rosa, 1 La Roja). He follows in the footsteps of Jonas Vingegaard, who won the Giro d’Italia this year after previous success at the Tour de France and La Vuelta. The other two active riders to have worn La Roja, the Maillot Jaune and the Maglia Rosa are participating in La Vuelta 26

guideposts.label: A gap of 1'42'' at km 70
guideposts.detail: So far, the race scenario aligns with the predictions of Kaden Groves (Alpecin-Premier Tech): "It’s gonna be a hard stage, up and down, always sort of twisty roads. It’s a tough stage, especially the final, but I expect a small breakaway controlled by Visma to try and take the red jersey with Van Aert. I expect a bunch sprint but it’s a super hard final so you have to see how the legs are."

guideposts.label: The gap is decreasing
guideposts.detail: The peloton reach km 80 with a gap of 1'20''.

guideposts.label: The average speed after 2 hours: 42.6 km/h
guideposts.detail: The gap has stabilised again: 1'30''.

guideposts.label: Halfway through the stage
guideposts.detail: The four leaders enter the final 100 kilometres with a gap down to 1'10''.

guideposts.label: The peloton is controlling the breakaway's efforts
45 seconds
guideposts.detail: Steven Kruijswijk (Visma-Lease a Bike) sets a strong pace with 75 kilometres to go.

guideposts.label: Coquard: "It is a great finish"
guideposts.detail: Along with Mads Pedersen, Bryan Coquard (Cofidis) is the other rider in the peloton who has already won in Manosque: “It is a great finish, where I’ve already won [in the Tour de la Provence 2022]. We’re really keen and highly motivated today. I think that was my first year with Cofidis. I’d won the Étoile de Bessèges ahead of Pedersen the week before. It’s a tough, grueling finish – just the sort

guideposts.label: Visma-Lease a Bike vs Hayter
guideposts.detail: Ethan Hayter (Soudal Quick-Step) has accelerated at the front of the lead group. Behind them, Bruno Armirail takes over the pace setting in the bunch.

guideposts.label: Chumil has crashed
guideposts.detail: Race doctors are with the Guatemalan rider to see if he can continue in the race.

guideposts.label: Into the final 50 kilometres
guideposts.detail: The fap is down 12'' with just under 15 kilometres to go to the bonus sprint.

guideposts.label: Chumil is the first rider out of La Vuelta 26
guideposts.detail: Sergio Chumil (Burgos Burpellet BH) couldn't resume racing after his crash.

guideposts.label: Hayter resists
guideposts.detail: The British rouleur has a lead of 30'' with 5 kilometres remaining to the intermediate sprint. He eyes the bonus seconds awarded on the line to take a decisive step towards La Roja.

guideposts.label: Hayter is caught
guideposts.detail: Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG) is at the very front of th peloton with 34 kilometres to go.

guideposts.label: Many trains at the front of the peloton
guideposts.detail: Visma-Lease a Bike, UAE Emirates XRG, Lidl-Trek, Groupama-FDJ United, Netcompany Ineos... These teams make the most of the width of the road to position their leaders at the front ahead of the final 10 kilometres.

guideposts.label: Van Aert attacks with 2 km to go
guideposts.detail: Pogacar tries to follow the Belgian!

guideposts.label: Top 5
guideposts.detail: 1. Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) 2. Pau Miquel (Bahrain Victorious) 3. Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG) 4. Mads Pedersen (Lidl-Trek) 5. Hugo Hofstetter (NSN)
